Golf is in populêre sport dy't in hege graad fan presyzje en feardigens freget. De golfbaan wurdt ferwachte dat se ûnderhâlden wurde nei in ûnbeholbere standert dy't it gebrûk fan spesjaliseare apparatuer fereasket. Fan 'e Fairway Turf Sweeper nei de sprayer fan golfbaan binne dizze masines in yntegraal diel fan it behâld fan jo golfbaan.

De Fairway Turf Sweeper is in essensjeel ark foar it hâlden fan jo golfbaan dy't liket op nij. Dizze masine is ûntworpen om gersknoppen effisjint te sweepjen en te ferwiderjen, blêden en oare pún dat it uterlik fan 'e kursus kin beynfloedzje. De fairway top dresser is in oare masine dy't kritysk is om de sûnens en uterlik fan jo gazon te behâlden. It wurdt brûkt om in tinne laach-boade of sân oan te passen oan in gazon om syn groeiende omstannichheden te ferbetterjen en sûne groei te befrijen.

In oare wichtige masine wurdt brûkt yn ûnderhâld fan golfbaan is de Greensand Topdresser. Dizze masine wurdt brûkt om sân oer it gazon te fersprieden om it oerflak te fersterkjen en de rôljende ôfstân fan 'e bal te fersterkjen. Sân-sifters wurde ek brûkt om te ferfangen en te sortearjen sân brûkt op golfbanen.

Foar hege ferkearskof, is de fairway Verti-snijder in essensjele masine. Dit ark wurdt brûkt om datch te ferwiderjen fan turf, dy't de bal rôlje kin beynfloedzje en putt. Fairway Lawn Borstels tsjinje in ferlykbere funksje, mar binne ûntworpen om ferwidering fan pún te tastean fan hurde oerflakken lykas paden en opritten.

Green Rollers wurde brûkt om ûnvolkomen te glêdjen yn golfbaan Turf, de masines helpe om in glêd en nivo spielfjild te meitsjen. Rollers binne foaral wichtich op golfbanen mei uneven griene oerflakken, om't se helpe om bal-rollôfstân te maksimalisearjen.

Ferfier is in oar wichtich aspekt fan it behâld fan in golfbaan, en auto-ferfier auto's wurde brûkt om minsken te ferfieren, masjine en materialen om 'e kursus te ferfieren. Dizze auto's binne foaral nuttich foar kursussen dy't in grut gebiet moatte dekke, tastean om rapper te ferfierjen oer it gebiet.

Uteinlik wurde golfbaansproeiers brûkt foar de kontroleare tapassing fan herbiziden, fungiciden, ynsektiziden en oare gemikaliën brûkt yn pestkontrôle. Dizze behannelingen helpe om de sûnens fan turf, beammen en oare fegetaasje te behâlden op 'e kursus.

Koartsein, it ûnderhâld fan golfbanen fereasket in searje sofistike en betroubere apparatuer en masines. Fan fairway gazon sweepers nei golfbaansproeiers, spielet elke masine in fitale rol yn it garandearjen fan dat kursussen wurde presinteare en ûnderhâlden en dat golfers harren genietsje. Anne JeffreysANNE JEFFREYS

by Bob Pontes and Boyd Magers

BP: What was your given name at birth?
AJ: Anne Jeffreys Carmichael. I was born in Goldsboro, NC, in 1923.
BP: What was your childhood like?
AJ: In spite of being a sickly child, it was most pleasant, due to a wonderful mother and superior grandparents.
BM: Hard to believe you were ever sickly. At 75 you look terrific.
AJ: Some people say ‘phooey’ to the golden years. But I say you can deter aging through diet, exercise and the right attitude. My mother started me on a lifetime routine of exercise, diet and vitamins. If you think young, dress youthfully, wear your hair in a becoming style, you can keep old age at bay. I also believe in living life by good thoughts—and in being kind to people.
BP: Why did you become an actress?
AJ: Mostly because my mother wanted a career in singing for me. Thank goodness she steered me on my path of destiny.My first film was a Buster Crabbe western. Then I went under contract to MGM and did “Tarzan’s New York Adventure” and “I Married an Angel” with my hero and heroine—Nelson Eddy and Jeanette McDonald. Then I went under contract to Republic and didn’t care for the roles of chorus girls or gangster molls they cast me in and requested to play a “nice girl role”—hence the Wild Bill Elliott series.

"Calling Wild Bill Elliott" lobby card ('43 Republic).

BM: Tell us your impressions of Bill.
AJ: A very nice gentleman. He was originally a dress extra and somebody talked him into doing the Red Ryder series—probably Pappy Yates who ran Republic. He was very tall—6'3", 6'4", and, of course, he had those boots, making him a giant. He was a man who knew what he wanted, smart business-wise. Everything was very well calculated and worked out in his career. He had it all planned what he was going to do and how he was going to do it. And he accomplished it. He became a big western star practically overnight. He was always sort of reserved and quiet, but fun…had a nice sense of humor. Of course, Gabby Hayes kept everything stirred up a bit. (Laughs) He was such a sweetheart. We had a lot of laughs together. I learned to steal scenes anyway I could because, usually, the girl in those things was very incidental. The back of my head was in most shots. I used to wear a bow ribbon in my hair, so I wiggled my bow ribbon, wiggled my ears…anything to throw them off and get a little action in the camera. Bill always appreciated it. During the series with Bill, I once had to play an Indian girl. (Laughs) They put a black wig on me, put dark makeup…‘course I had blue eyes. Put a headband around my forehead with a feather, buckskins and moccasins. The first day with all this getup on I went in the commissary and was at the counter when my agent came in and sat right down beside me. I thought—he doesn’t recognize me, so I didn’t say anything. We must have eaten lunch beside each other for 15-20 minutes until I finally said, “Could you pass the salt please?”  He  looked around and gasped—“Annie?” Another thing—the crew were great pranksters. They were mischievous. I was the only girl and we were working in a phony cave on the backlot. It was one of those hot, dusty days. My name in the film (“Wagon Tracks West”) was Moonhush. (Laughs) I was sitting in this canvas chair and did not see the cowboy sneak up behind me and tie my Indian fringe from my buckskins to the chair. Then someone hollered, “Annie, they want you over here. Hurry, hurry.” I got up and took the chair with me! Here I was walking along dragging the chair behind me tied to the fringe of my buckskin! Another joke they played on me…wearing these big old moccasins I was always slipping my feet out and putting on comfortable shoes. They took them one time, put them behind my chair, then hollered, “Come on Annie, they want you now. Put on your moccasins.” I jumped into my moccasins and, unknowingly, they had filled them with talcum powder. Every time I stepped, these big white puffs (Laughs) came flying all over the place. Whitecloud Moonhush they called me after that! Still another time, the Indians were in the cave supposedly drying fish over the fire and they had these smoked herring. Somebody took one of these smoked herring and put it in my Indian knapsack! It was a hot day and—phew, I couldn’t figure out where the fish was. They’re all walkin’ ‘round holding their noses—“Eeeuck—Annie!” It wasn’t until lunch when I took the knapsack off that I realized what they’d done. I took it and hid it in the prop box but didn’t tell the wranglers where I put it. I said, “I found the fish fellas…one of you has it in your knapsack.” They searched all day! “Annie—now this isn’t funny anymore, it’s real hot out here and that fish is smelling up something somewhere.” I said, “No, no, you’ve got to find it.” For three days I let that fish foul up the prop box. (Laughs) It was a lot of fun.

Anne as Indian girl Moonhush in "Wagon Tracks West" ('43 Republic).

BP: You starred with Randolph Scott in “Return Of the Badmen” which had an all star cast. Of them all, who stands out in your mind?
AJ: Gabby was an old friend from Republic, and Randy Scott, a fellow North Carolinian, was a true gentleman; but Robert Ryan is the one I remember most vividly. He was a very intense actor and murdered my character in both “Trail Street” and “Return Of the Badmen”. He choked me to death in one and shot me in the back in the other. He seemed to enjoy it, so I was a little leery of him. (Laughs) However, he really was a very nice, warm person and a terrific actor.

Randolph Scott, Madge Meredith and Robert Ryan in "Trail Street" ('47 RKO). Anne and Scott are on the left edge of this lobby card.

BP: What are the things you will always remember about making western films?
AJ: The dust and dirt—and reflectors blinding me.
BP: What were the differences you found between making a low budget western and a big budget western?
AJ: Mostly you had more rehearsal time. Basically, they were the same—same horses, same wranglers, a lot of the same locations and a lot of the same actors. I enjoyed “Nevada”. I liked working with Mitchum and I had a good role for a western. We worked on location, a beautiful spot near Mt. Whitney. We stayed in Lone Pine.

"Death Valley Manhunt" title card.

BP: What does being an actress mean to you?
AJ: All I desire—in my professional life. I hope to continue acting as long as God allows me to.
BP: What are the mistakes you made about your career?
AJ: Not being demanding enough or too choosy of my roles. I enjoyed acting, so I’d do any role the studio came up with.
BM: But best days of your life were on Broadway.
AJ: I did five Broadway shows. My first was “Street Scene”—opera really. I was under contract to RKO but fell in love with N.Y. theatre. Then I did an operetta written especially for me. I did “Kiss Me Kate” for two years, then “Three Wishes For Jamie”. After that “Kismet” with Alfred Drake at the Lincoln Center. I had about ten good years on Broadway, but kept going back to do films. When I left North Carolina, I studied music in N.Y. I was trained in opera and sang with the municipal opera company in N.Y. as a 15 year old. I’m proud of all my stage work which includes dozens of different shows, including “The King and I”, “Camelot”, “Sound of Music”, “Carousel”, “Destry” and “Bells Are Ringing”.
BP: Was “Topper” the only TV series you and your husband, Robert Sterling, made?
AJ: We followed it with “Love That Jill” which was about the high fashion world. It only ran one season. He’s done other series—“Ichabod and Me”, which he hated. I did “The Delphi Bureau” and one season on “Falcon Crest”. I was on “Finder of Lost Loves”, an ABC night time series. I had a running part on the daytime soap, “General Hospital”. My husband no longer acts. I’ve also been on “Baywatch” recently. I love to travel and have done a lot of it. I have a wonderful husband and three great sons, and, at present count, three darling grandchildren. God has blessed me!

At 94, Anne died in L.A. September 27, 2017.

Bill Elliott, Jack Kirk, Tom London, Gabby Hayes, Nancy Gay and Anne Jeffreys in a tense moment from "Overland Mail Robbery" ('43 Republic).

Core Components of a Hydraulic System: Structure and Functions of the Cab Cylinder and Hydraulic Pump 2025-12-03 09:10:38

Core Components of Hydraulic Systems: Cab Cylinder and Hydraulic Pump

In industrial machinery, hydraulic systems have become indispensable due to their high efficiency, quick response, and adaptability to various working conditions. Among these systems, the key components that drive vehicle operation include the hydraulic cylinder and the hydraulic pump. These essential elements generate working pressure, transmit power to the load, and complete specific operational tasks.

Hydraulic Cylinder

The hydraulic cylinder serves as the actuator within the hydraulic system. It relies on internal pressure changes to extend or retract the piston rod, thereby pushing the vehicle forward or backward. Its design typically follows principles of compact structure, light weight, wear resistance, and ease of installation and maintenance.
The basic components include the cylinder barrel (with a smooth inner surface), piston rod, sealing rings, guide bushings, and counterweights. When hydraulic oil enters the cylinder, the pressure drives the piston rod to move, which in turn propels the wheels. Additionally, to ensure operational safety, the cylinder is equipped with safety valves to prevent overload conditions.

Hydraulic Pump

The hydraulic pump acts as the “heart” of the hydraulic system, with its primary function being to provide stable hydraulic power during operation. Depending on application requirements, pumps can be categorized into gear pumps, vane pumps, plunger pumps, and more. Each type offers unique advantages for different operating environments. For example, gear pumps have a simple structure and low cost, making them suitable for small-flow, high-pressure applications; vane pumps, due to their compact and lightweight design, are widely used in small engineering machinery.

Function Analysis

Functions of the Cylinder:
The hydraulic cylinder's main role is to control the vehicle’s movement direction through the extension and retraction of the piston rod. When acceleration or deceleration is needed, the driver adjusts the throttle to change oil pressure, thereby altering the output torque of the cylinder and regulating vehicle speed.

Functions of the Pump:
The hydraulic pump continuously supplies high-pressure oil to the entire hydraulic system, ensuring that the cylinder and other components receive the necessary power. Its presence enables the system to self-adjust and maintain stable and efficient operation even under varying load conditions.

In conclusion, both the cab cylinder and hydraulic pump are critical and irreplaceable parts of the hydraulic system. Working together, they ensure stable vehicle operation in complex environments, improve work efficiency, and safeguard operator safety. For modern engineering vehicles pursuing higher perforMANce and intelligence, selecting high-quality cylinders and pumps is key to achieving superior overall performance.

De tentoanstellingsguod sille 16 kategoryen omfetsje, dy't leveransiers fan hege kwaliteit út ferskate yndustryen en binnen- en bûtenlânske keapers byinoar bringe.

data.text:
English

De ynfloed fan ferstjoerpriisfluktuaasjes op 'e slangklemmenyndustry

Resinte gegevens fan 'e Shanghai Aviation Exchange litte wichtige ferskowingen sjen yn 'e Shanghai Export Containerized Freight Index (SCFI), mei gefolgen foar de slangklemmenyndustry. Yn 'e ôfrûne wike hat de SCFI in wichtige delgong meimakke fan 17,22 punten, en berikt 1013,78 punten. Dit markearret de twadde wyklikse daling fan 'e yndeks op rige, wêrby't it delgongstempo útwreidet fan 1,2% nei 1,67%. It is opmerklik dat, wylst de rûte fan it Fiere Easten nei de westkust fan 'e Feriene Steaten in beskieden tanimming seach, oare wichtige rûtes in delgong meimakken.

Spesifyk is it frachttaryf per FEU (fjirtich-foet lykweardige ienheid) op 'e line fan it Fiere Easten nei de Westkust fan Amearika mei US$ 3 omheech gien nei US$ 2006, wat in wyklikse tanimming fan 0,14% oanjout. Omkeard seach it frachttaryf op 'e line fan it Fiere Easten nei de Amerikaanske eastkust in wichtige daling fan US$ 58 nei US$ 3.052 per FEU, wat in wyklikse daling fan 1,86% wjerspegelt. Lykas ek de line fan it Fiere Easten nei Europa seach in wichtige daling, wêrby't it frachttaryf per TEU (tweintich-foet lykweardige ienheid) mei US$ 50 sakke nei US$ 802, wat in wyklikse daling fan 5,86% fertsjintwurdiget. Derneist ûnderfûn de line fan it Fiere Easten nei de Middellânske See in daling fan frachttariven, mei in daling fan US$ 45 nei US$ 1.455 per TEU, wat in daling fan 2,77% betsjut.

Yn it ljocht fan dizze fluktuaasjes,Dinsen, as in wichtige spiler yn 'e hannels-eksportsektor, bliuwt wach by it kontrolearjen fan feroaringen yn ferstjoerprizen. Us oanbod fan populêre produkten, ynklusyfgasklemmen, útlaatklemmen, slangklemmen en earclips, binne ûnderwurpen oan 'e ynfloed fan dizze ferskowingen. Wy moedigje klanten oan om kontakt mei ús op te nimmen foar fierdere ynformaasje of oerlis as nedich. Bliuw op 'e hichte en ferbûn mei Dinsen foar de lêste updates oer ferstjoertrends en har gefolgen foar ús produkten.
